member.name: T:BimGo.Bridge.RevitEditor
member.summary:
Applies walkthrough edits to one Revit document. Each request runs in its own transaction named "BimGo: …" (one undo step each) with warnings swallowed and errors rolled back. Revit API thread only; the session's ExternalEvent handler () calls for live edits and (RevitEditor.Push.cs) for a file's journal. Nothing here throws to the caller.
Phases: demolition sets Phase Demolished to the session's "new" phase and only accepts elements that exist in the "existing" phase; copies are created in the new phase.

Pushing a standalone file's journal into the model (journal.apply).
The whole push runs in one ("BimGo: Push N edits from file.bimgo") that is assimilated, so one Ctrl+Z in Revit undoes it all; each entry still gets its own transaction so one failure doesn't sink the rest. A dry run does exactly the same work, then rolls the group back: what it reports is what the real push would do, including clones of clones.
Targets are found by UniqueId (stable across saves, upgrades and local copies); clones made by the push are tracked by their clone key. Moves and clones check that the element is still where it was when the file was made (a conflict otherwise).

member.name: T:BimGo.Extraction.SceneExtractor
member.summary: Builds the immutable snapshot from the active Revit document. Runs on the Revit API thread only. Converts feet to metres and shifts everything to a scene-local origin (rounded to whole metres) so float precision holds up on large sites.

Round X-B2: records every Planting and Entourage instance in the extraction's scope (the host and the ticked links; what the active view shows when extracting the active view only), whether or not their categories' geometry is extracted, so the walkthrough can swap them for billboards: UniqueId, family and type, base point, size, and the extracted element when there is one.

Grids round A: the grids of the host and of each extracted link (through its transform), for the walkthrough's grid overlay. Each grid keeps its name, its plan line (lines as two points, arcs tessellated, multi-segment grids joined into one line) and its 3D vertical extent. Read-only; a grid that can't be read is skipped and logged.

The family library (next round): the loadable family types the walkthrough's Place gun can place.
Types: every loaded in the host model whose category is a ticked FFE or services category (so a placed instance is drawn), in-place families excluded, capped at (types already used in the model first).
Previews: Revit's own type preview (), as a small PNG.
Geometry: for level-based and work-plane / face-based types (on the level's plane, see ): one temporary instance of each on the lowest level, in a single transaction that is always rolled back (nothing stays in the model, nothing enters the undo list). Each is extracted like any element (materials, glow, light), then becomes a hidden template at the tail of the snapshot, moved below the model so an older BimGo that draws it anyway draws it out of sight.
Live sessions only (Go / refresh): Export .bimgo never calls it. Any failure leaves the library smaller or empty; the walkthrough is never affected.

Artificial lighting capture: which surfaces glow and where lighting fixtures emit light.
Glow comes from a material's Revit self-illumination (Generic "Self Illumination" luminance, filter colour and colour temperature; Advanced / Physical "Emission"), anywhere in the model. Inside Lighting Fixtures elements, materials whose name contains one of glow too, and a raised fixture with neither gets its bottom, downward-facing faces as a guessed lens.
Lights: one per Lighting Fixtures element, at the centre of its glowing surface (just in front of it), pointing the way that surface faces; output and colour temperature from the fixture's parameters when they can be read ("Initial Intensity", "Initial Color"…), else estimated.
Everything here is best effort: a failure leaves the element unlit, never fails the extraction.

Materials round: render colours, textures and surface coordinates for the walkthrough's Realistic mode. Only runs when is ticked; otherwise nothing here does any work and the snapshot is exactly as before.
Table: one per material used (per document). The colour and texture slot depend on the appearance schema: Generic generic_diffuse (+ image fade), Advanced opaque_albedo, Metal metal_f0, Layered layered_diffuse, Hardwood hardwood_color, and the simple schemas' *_color. Prism surface_albedo is the reflection map and is never used as colour.
Textures: the bitmap on the colour slot is found with (absolute → Autodesk library → Revit's additional render appearance paths → model folder), downscaled to the size cap, re-encoded as JPEG and embedded once per image. Images are cached for the Revit session, so a live refresh (F5) only reads new ones.
Surface coordinates: metres along each face's own axes. Planar walls get U horizontal and V up, floors and roofs get plan X / Y (so coursing and boards line up across faces); curved faces use the face's parameters scaled to metres; free meshes are box-mapped.
Everything is best effort: a failure leaves a material untextured (its colour still shows), never fails the extraction.

Round Z-A: every non-empty instance parameter of a room for the walkthrough's room data overlay (tags, the parameter picker and the target check): the display text as Revit shows it, and a number in the model's display units where the value is numeric (doubles converted from internal units, integers as they are, text read for a leading number), so "Area" and a "Required area" compare in the same units. Read-only; unreadable parameters are left out.
